topics.title: Surface area and volume of solids

learn.hook: Ice-cream cones, cricket balls and gas cylinders — every solid has a 'skin' (surface area) and a 'filling' (volume)!
points: Cuboid: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), volume = lbh. Cube: TSA = 6a², volume = a³.
Cylinder: curved surface area (CSA) = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(r + h), volume = πr²h.
Cone: slant height l = √(r² + h²), CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(l + r), volume = ⅓πr²h.
Sphere: surface area = 4πr², volume = (4/3)πr³. Hemisphere: CSA = 2πr², TSA = 3πr², volume = (2/3)πr³.
Surface area is in square units (cm²); volume is in cubic units (cm³).

example.q: Find the volume of a cone with radius 7 cm and height 12 cm. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: A painter needs surface area to buy paint for a water tank, and a milkman needs volume to know how much milk his can holds.

games.title: Match the formula
pairs: Curved surface area of a cone
Total surface area of a hemisphere

quiz.q: A cone has radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. What is its slant height?
quiz.mistake: Adds r and h (14 cm) instead of using Pythagoras

quiz.q: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm?
quiz.mistake: Uses r² instead of r³, or forgets the 4/3

quiz.q: What is the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Includes the two circular ends (TSA = 748 cm²)

quiz.q: What is the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: TSA = curved part 2πr² + flat circle πr² = 3πr² = 3 × 154 = 462 cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses only the curved part 2πr² = 308 cm²

quiz.q: What is the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ⅓ and gives the cylinder's volume

quiz.q: What is the total surface area of a cube with edge 5 cm?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 square faces: 6 × 5² = 150 cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses only 4 faces (100 cm²) or gives the volume (125)

quiz.q: A cylinder and a cone have the same base radius and the same height. What is the ratio of their volumes (cylinder : cone)?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = πr²h and cone = ⅓πr²h, so the cylinder holds 3 times as much.
quiz.mistake: Writes the ratio the wrong way round

quiz.q: A round laddoo is a sphere of radius 2 cm. What is its surface area?
quiz.explain: 4πr² = 4 × π × 4 = 16π cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses the volume formula and gets 32π/3

teach.ask: Gappu holds an ice-cream cone: 'What's the difference between its surface area and its volume?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Surface area covers the outside in square units; volume fills the inside in cubic units!
teach.nudge: Which one is about covering and which is about filling — and what units does each use?

learn.hook: A toy top is a cone stuck on a hemisphere — to paint it, count only the surfaces you can actually touch!
points: A combined solid is made by joining two or more basic solids.
Its surface area = sum of the surfaces that remain visible on the outside.
Faces that are glued together are hidden, so they are NOT counted.
So the surface area of a combination is usually LESS than the sum of the separate total surface areas.
Draw a sketch and list each exposed part before adding.

example.q: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 3 m with a cone of slant height 10 m on top. How much canvas is needed (no floor)? (π = 22/7)
steps: Floor and joined circles are not canvas

learn.reallife: Tent makers at a mela, toy makers and painters of temple domes all work out only the visible surface.

games.title: Visible or hidden?
items: When a cone sits on a hemisphere, the cone's circular base is not part of the outer surface.
It is glued to the hemisphere's flat face and hidden.
The surface area of a combined solid is the sum of the TSAs of its parts.
The joined faces are hidden, so they must be left out.
The surface of a capsule = two hemispheres + the curved surface of a cylinder.
The flat ends are hidden where the parts join.
To paint the outside of a hemispherical dome, you paint 2πr².
Only the curved part is outside; the flat base sits on the building.
Two identical cubes joined face to face have total surface area 12a².
If a hemisphere is scooped out of the top of a cylinder, the inside curved surface 2πr² is added.
The hollow bowl surface is new, while the top circle is removed.

items.text: Cone on a hemisphere: surface = πrl + ___
Two cubes of edge 4 cm joined face to face: surface area = ___ cm²
Tent without floor = curved surface of cylinder + ___

quiz.q: Two cubes of edge 5 cm are joined end to end. What is the surface area of the cuboid formed?
quiz.explain: Each cube has 6 faces of 25 cm²; joining hides 2 faces. 10 × 25 = 250 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the two TSAs (300 cm²) without removing the hidden faces

quiz.q: A capsule is a cylinder of length 10 cm and radius 3.5 cm with a hemisphere on each end. What is its surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder curved part = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 10 = 220 cm². Two hemispheres = 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 12.25 = 154 cm². Total = 374 cm².
quiz.mistake: Counts the hemispheres twice over or adds the hidden ends

quiz.q: A toy is a cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm on a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. What is its total surface area?
quiz.explain: Slant height = 5 cm, so cone CSA = π × 3 × 5 = 15π. Hemisphere CSA = 2π × 9 = 18π. Total = 33π cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses the hemisphere's TSA (3πr²) and gets 42π

quiz.q: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 5 m topped by a cone of slant height 9 m. How much canvas is needed (no floor)? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder walls = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 5 = 220 m². Cone = 22/7 × 7 × 9 = 198 m². Total = 418 m².
quiz.mistake: Adds the floor (154 m²) as well

quiz.q: A hemisphere is fixed on top of a cylinder of the same radius. Which surfaces are hidden?
options: The curved surface of the cylinder
The flat face of the hemisphere and the top of the cylinder
quiz.explain: The flat circle of the hemisphere sits exactly on the top circle of the cylinder, so both are hidden.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bottom base is hidden because it sits on the table

quiz.q: A cube of edge 14 cm has a hemisphere of diameter 14 cm fixed on top. What is the surface area of the solid? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cube = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm². The hemisphere adds 2πr² but covers πr² of the top, a net gain of πr² = 154 cm². Total = 1330 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds 2πr² but forgets that it covers part of the cube's top

quiz.q: A solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm has a hemisphere of the same radius scooped out from its top. What is the total surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Curved side 440 + bottom circle 154 + inside bowl 2πr² = 308. The top circle is gone. Total = 902 cm².
quiz.mistake: Keeps the top circle that was scooped away

quiz.q: A Diwali lamp-shade model is a cone (radius 7 cm, slant height 25 cm) on a hollow cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 6 cm), open at the bottom. What is its outer surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cone = 22/7 × 7 × 25 = 550 cm². Cylinder side = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 6 = 264 cm². Total = 814 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the open bottom circle (154 cm²)

teach.ask: Gappu glued a cone onto a hemisphere: 'Do I just add both total surface areas to paint it?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Add only the visible surfaces — the glued parts don't need paint!
teach.nudge: What happens to the faces that are stuck together?

learn.hook: How much ice-cream fits in a cone with a scoop on top? Just add the volumes!
points: Volume of a combined solid = sum of the volumes of its parts (they don't overlap).
If a part is cut out or scooped away, subtract its volume.
Unlike surface area, no volume is 'hidden' when solids are joined.
Keep the answer in terms of π when the question allows — it avoids rounding errors.

example.q: An ice-cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 6 cm, with a hemisphere of ice-cream of radius 3 cm on top. Find the total volume.

learn.reallife: Dairy workers and gas companies find the volume of capsule-shaped tankers this way to know how much they can carry.

items.q: Volume of a cylinder, r = 7 cm, h = 2 cm (cm³)
Volume of a cone, r = 7 cm, h = 3 cm (cm³)
Volume of a cube of edge 4 cm (cm³)
Two cubes of edge 3 cm joined: volume (cm³)
Cuboid 10 × 5 × 4 cm with a 2 cm cube cut out: volume (cm³)

games.title: Smallest volume to largest
games.prompt: All have radius 3 cm; height 3 cm where needed

quiz.q: An ice-cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm, filled and topped with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. What is the total volume of ice-cream?
quiz.explain: Cone = ⅓π × 9 × 4 = 12π. Hemisphere = (2/3)π × 27 = 18π. Total = 30π cm³.
quiz.mistake: Uses a full sphere (36π) instead of a hemisphere

quiz.q: A solid is a cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 6 cm) with a cone of the same radius and height 6 cm on top. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder = 22/7 × 49 × 6 = 924 cm³. Cone = ⅓ × 924 = 308 cm³. Total = 1232 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Treats the cone as having the same volume as the cylinder

quiz.q: A capsule is a cylinder of radius 3 cm and length 10 cm with a hemisphere at each end. What is its volume?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = π × 9 × 10 = 90π. Two hemispheres make a sphere = (4/3)π × 27 = 36π. Total = 126π cm³.
quiz.mistake: Adds only one hemisphere (108π)

quiz.q: A cone of the same base and height is carved out of a solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. What volume is left?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = π × 9 × 5 = 45π. Cone = ⅓ × 45π = 15π. Remaining = 30π cm³ (two-thirds of the cylinder).
quiz.mistake: Gives the cone's volume instead of what is left

quiz.q: A wooden toy is a hemisphere of radius 7 cm topped with a cone of the same radius and height 7 cm. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Gives the volume of only one part

quiz.q: Two cubes, each of volume 27 cm³, are joined end to end. What is the volume of the cuboid formed?
quiz.explain: No volume is lost when solids are joined, so 27 + 27 = 54 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Thinks joining hides some volume, as it does for surface area

quiz.q: Why can we add the volumes of the parts but not their total surface areas?
options: Joined faces are hidden from the surface, but all the space inside still counts
Volume is always bigger than surface area
Surface area is measured in cm³
We can add both in every case
quiz.explain: When solids are joined, the touching faces disappear from the outside, but none of the space inside is lost.
quiz.mistake: Treats surface area and volume the same way

quiz.q: Harpreet's water bottle is a cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 20 cm. How much water does it hold? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Volume = 22/7 × 12.25 × 20 = 770 cm³. Since 1 L = 1000 cm³, that is 0.77 L.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 1000 when converting to litres

teach.ask: Gappu stuck a scoop of ice-cream on a cone: 'How much ice-cream is there altogether?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Find the volume of each part and add them. That's a lot of ice-cream!
teach.nudge: What do I find for each part, and how do I combine them?
